slides.title: Follow one result through several different contracts
keyPoints: Source semantics define valid behavior
Build stages produce different artifacts
Execution combines mappings, instructions, and system interfaces
slides.narration: The byte-summary utility connects much of the course in one path. Source types define valid bytes and arithmetic. The compiler and assembler create machine code and relocation information. The linker resolves the pieces, and the loader establishes a process image before main begins. Running instructions then consume valid input supplied by read and eventually format output for write. A failure at any one boundary can stop the whole job even when the checksum formula is correct. Our aim is to trace the responsibilities precisely, rather than treating compilation, loading, execution, and hardware I/O as one indistinct action.

slides.title: Source state gives the optimizer a behavior to preserve
keyPoints: A global scale begins at seven
The same function returns 21, then 27 after a change
The source does not require a particular instruction count
slides.narration: The program defines one global integer and one function that multiplies an argument by its current value. The first call with three returns twenty-one. Main changes the global to nine, so the second call returns twenty-seven. These are the required observable results for this single-threaded program. An optimizing compiler may inline the function or calculate known values ahead of time; the source does not promise that each call becomes a machine call or each expression reloads memory. The example makes the distinction concrete: source semantics constrain behavior, while assembly reveals one permitted implementation chosen for a build.

slides.title: A counted byte range is different from a C string
keyPoints: A null byte can be ordinary binary data
strlen stops at the first null terminator
A counted view processes exactly its stated extent
slides.narration: The four-byte array contains A, a null byte, B, and a final null terminator. strlen sees the first null and reports one byte of C-string text. The counted string_view deliberately covers the first three bytes, including the embedded null, and its unsigned-byte traversal produces a sum of one hundred thirty-one. The static assertion makes the ASCII character-value assumption explicit. This is a computation and representation demo, not file I/O. When read returns three bytes, a binary processor must use that count; applying a text terminator rule can silently discard valid input after a zero byte.

slides.title: The build stages fail for different reasons
keyPoints: Preprocessing finds headers and expands macros
Compilation applies language and target rules
Assembly emits object code; linking resolves definitions
slides.narration: Saving source creates text, not an executable. Preprocessing can fail because a header is missing. Compilation can reject an incompatible type or invalid language construct. The assembler encodes target instructions and produces a relocatable object with symbols and relocation records. Linking then resolves references against definitions in other objects and libraries. A missing checksum_update definition belongs at the link boundary, not inside the byte loop. Keep artifacts in a known build directory and inspect the stage that failed. Running an older executable after a failed build can otherwise produce convincing output from code you did not just compile.

slides.title: Where the simple approach fails
keyPoints: Seeing the correct output alone does not tell you which functions were inlined, which pages faulted, or how many system calls occurred.
A related failure in the generalized operation is concrete: Use strlen on the binary input. It stops at the first zero byte and reports zero rather than two.
The repair changes the operation at the point where the rule can be enforced: Carry an explicit byte count and iterate the whole valid range. Keep text terminators separate from binary framing.

slides.title: Loader → Virtual Address Space
slides.eyebrow: SOURCE CONCEPT · REASON THROUGH THE MECHANISM
keyPoints: The executable’s loadable segments become virtual mappings with appropriate permissions and backing.
Code, initialized data, zero-filled storage, stack, and libraries occupy regions of the process’s address space.
The loader need not eagerly copy every executable byte into physical memory before execution begins.
File-backed demand paging and shared mappings allow work to occur as pages are used.
slides.narration:
The executable’s loadable segments become virtual mappings with appropriate permissions and backing. Code, initialized data, zero-filled storage, stack, and libraries occupy regions of the process’s address space. The loader need not eagerly copy every executable byte into physical memory before execution begins. File-backed demand paging and shared mappings allow work to occur as pages are used. The address-space layout is therefore a mapping plan, not simply a complete physical-memory photograph. [ R10 , R14 ]

In plain English: Think of an address written on a note: the note can tell you where to look, but it does not prove the thing is still there or that you are allowed to use it.

slides.title: CPU → Registers and Caches
slides.eyebrow: SOURCE CONCEPT · REASON THROUGH THE MECHANISM
keyPoints: The byte-sum loop uses registers for pointers, counters, and partial results where the compiler chooses.
Loads obtain input bytes through the cache hierarchy.
Several adjacent bytes can share a fetched line, giving spatial locality.
Calling the update function may require arguments in the ABI’s designated registers and preservation of callee-saved state.
slides.narration:
The byte-sum loop uses registers for pointers, counters, and partial results where the compiler chooses. Loads obtain input bytes through the cache hierarchy. Several adjacent bytes can share a fetched line, giving spatial locality. Calling the update function may require arguments in the ABI’s designated registers and preservation of callee-saved state. Inlining can remove that call boundary but not the source-level requirement to read only valid input bytes. Machine optimization and memory safety remain separate obligations.

In plain English: A cache is like keeping the things you use most often on your desk instead of walking to a storage room every time.

slides.title: Build and trace a complete byte-summary utility
slides.eyebrow: SOURCE CONCEPT · REASON THROUGH THE MECHANISM
keyPoints: The public interface states that data designates at least length valid bytes whenever length is nonzero.
The function borrows the bytes and retains no pointer.
Companion listing: ch60/checksum.h
Companion listing: ch60/checksum.c
slides.narration:
The public interface states that data designates at least length valid bytes whenever length is nonzero. The function borrows the bytes and retains no pointer. Companion listing: ch60/checksum.h Companion listing: ch60/checksum.c Companion listing: ch60/main.c From the chapter’s source directory, the following commands expose separate stages. They write only local build products; use a copy or dedicated build directory for experimentation. The final output is bytes=4 sum=208 . The shell starts a producer and connects it to the utility through a pipe. The utility’s read returns valid bytes, the checksum function processes that exact extent, and a complete-transfer write emits the formatted result. A failure at any stage has a different meaning. Preprocessing can fail to find a header. Compilation can reject a type error. Linking can miss a definition. Loading can fail to locate a runtime dependency. Reading can fail on an invalid descriptor. The checksum itself can remain logically correct while the overall program fails to receive or deliver data. An integrated diagnosis identifies the failed boundary before changing unrelated code.

slides.title: Declarations and ABI agreements must match across pieces
keyPoints: A header states the shared interface
A definition supplies the implementation
Successful symbol resolution is weaker than a correct calling contract
slides.narration: The source byte-summary example separates a header, a checksum implementation, and a driver. The header lets each translation unit agree on parameter types and return type before linking. A manually invented declaration can still be incompatible with the actual definition, even if the linker finds the same symbol name under the platform's conventions. The application binary interface, or ABI, includes how arguments and results travel at the machine boundary. Use the intended headers and compatible build settings rather than guessing a signature. A successful link establishes resolution, not every semantic or calling-convention promise.

question.prompt: Why is copying only a library function’s name insufficient when declaring it manually?
question.answer: Its parameter types, return type, linkage, and calling convention must agree with the definition. A found symbol does not prove that agreement.

slides.title: The loader prepares mappings before main runs
keyPoints: Executable segments have permissions and backing
Startup code and dynamic loading can run first
Demand paging avoids eagerly copying every byte into RAM
slides.narration: Starting the executable asks the operating system to establish the program image. Loadable segments become virtual mappings for code, initialized data, zero-filled storage, and other regions. Dynamically linked programs also involve runtime loading according to the platform. main is normally reached only after startup code has established language-runtime state. A missing required library can therefore stop the program before its first line. The mapped address space is not a photograph of physical memory: file-backed demand paging can supply pages as they are used. This separates loader obligations from later page faults, cache behavior, and source-level object rules.
actions: Ask learners to predict the answer and state their assumptions.
Reveal the answer, then identify which program boundary establishes it.

question.prompt: Why can a program fail before the first statement of main?
question.answer: Executable loading, runtime dependency resolution, or startup initialization may fail before control reaches main.

slides.title: One load crosses distinct translation and storage mechanisms
keyPoints: Virtual addresses need translation
TLB misses are different from cache misses
Page faults are not ordinary cache misses
slides.narration: The checksum loop reads through a pointer, but the processor and memory system perform several different jobs below that expression. Address translation finds the relevant mapping, often using cached translations in the TLB. Data caches supply nearby bytes when present. A data-cache miss may fetch from another cache or memory without a page fault. A page fault involves the operating system because the access needs mapping or residency handling, or is invalid. Sequential traversal can exploit spatial locality because adjacent bytes share cache lines. Keep these events separate when explaining why a loop waits; they suggest different evidence and remedies.
actions: Ask learners to predict the answer and state their assumptions.
Reveal the answer, then identify which program boundary establishes it.

question.prompt: Does a cache miss necessarily mean the operating system loads a page from storage?
question.answer: No. A cache miss often fetches from another cache or resident main memory. Page faults and storage I/O are separate events.

slides.title: A read result becomes the next memory-safety boundary
keyPoints: A 4096-byte buffer may receive only 100 bytes
Process the positive returned extent exactly
EOF and error do not supply another full buffer
slides.narration: The source utility uses a buffer that can hold four thousand ninety-six bytes, but read may return any positive count up to the requested size. If it returns one hundred, only those one hundred bytes are the newly supplied input for the next checksum update. Processing the full capacity would include unrelated or stale bytes. A zero result has EOF meaning for this stream workflow, while an error requires its own handling. This is a crucial cross-layer connection: an operating-system return value becomes a language-level valid range. Passing that exact count keeps the computation independent of whether input came from a file or pipe.
actions: Ask learners to predict the answer and state their assumptions.

question.prompt: Why is summing all 4096 buffer positions wrong after read returns 100?
question.answer: Only the returned 100-byte extent is valid new input. Capacity is not the amount of data obtained.

slides.title: Kernel entry, blocking, and context switching are separate
keyPoints: A system call enters kernel code
Available data may let it return promptly
Waiting can let another task run
Cached I/O may not reach a device
slides.narration: A write wrapper arranges arguments according to the operating-system interface and enters the kernel. That entry is not automatically a switch to another process. The kernel may complete the request immediately, or block while waiting and let another task run. Similarly, a read may be satisfied from available cached data without asking a physical device to transfer anything new. Drivers, DMA, interrupts, and device queues can participate when needed, but their activity is not visible as one fixed sequence for every call. Diagnose the chosen input endpoint and return behavior before attributing all time to a CPU loop or disk.

question.prompt: Does every system call imply a context switch to another process?
question.answer: No. Kernel entry can return without blocking or scheduling another task. Those are separate events.

slides.title: Diagnose the earliest failed boundary in the end-to-end path
keyPoints: Build error, load error, read error, and wrong sum differ
Keep the sequential checksum as a reference
Check output completion as carefully as input
slides.narration: If the program prints the wrong total, first ask whether the built executable is current, whether read supplied the intended bytes, and whether the checksum saw the exact extent. If nothing prints, the error may instead be loading, an invalid descriptor, formatting, or incomplete output delivery. A correct arithmetic function cannot repair a broken surrounding pipeline. Record build commands, input bytes, exit status, standard error, and actual output so each boundary is reviewable. The next capstone adds concurrency to this path while retaining the sequential reference, because integrating more mechanisms increases the number of promises that must agree.
